docs.title: Link pins
docs.text: Pins are points a link is drawn through. They are part of the model, saved with the link, and every change to them is a command, so they follow the same rules as the rest of the stage. This page describes the pieces, for people working on Nyx or on tools that read and write stages.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Link.pins (in nyx.core.link) is a list of QtCore.QPointF in graph coordinates, from the source of the link to its target. The property returns copies, so changing the list doesn't change the link. Setting it replaces the pins and emits Stage.link_pins_changed(link_uuid).

from PySide6 import QtCore
from nyx.api.v1 import commands

link = stage.get_object(link_uuid)
stage.push_command(
    commands.SetLinkPinsCommand(stage, link, [QtCore.QPointF(300.0, -80.0)])
)

Always change pins with SetLinkPinsCommand, not by setting Link.pins, unless you are restoring state inside another command. The command stores the old pins for undo. It replaces the whole list, so adding, moving and removing a pin are the same command with a different list. Its target_nodes are the two nodes the link connects, so it is refused for links inside a referenced stage. It doesn't set MODIFIES_STRUCTURE.

A command that removes and recreates links has to carry the pins itself, because recreating a link only gives it its ends and uuid. UnlinkNodeComponentsCommand does: it reads the pins in redo and sets them again in undo. Do the same in a new command of that kind. Commands that go through serialization, like deleting a node, get them for free.

docs.title: File format
docs.text:
Link.serialize writes the pins under a pins key as a list of [x, y], after source_uuid and target_uuid:

{
  "source_uuid": "...",
  "target_uuid": "...",
  "pins": [[100.0, 80.0], [300.0, -80.0]]
}

The key is left out for a link without pins, so files without pins are unchanged. Link.deserialize reads it with an empty default, so older files load.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
Piece Where Role build_link_path editor/graphics/link_path.py Takes the pins too. It builds each part between two points with the path builder of the style and joins them. find_pin_index editor/graphics/link_path.py Finds where a new pin goes: the part of the link that passes closest to a point. GraphicsLinkPin editor/graphics/graphics_link_pin.py The dot. A movable child of GraphicsLink. It redraws the link while it moves and asks the link to push the move when the mouse is released. GraphicsLink editor/graphics/graphics_link.py Owns the pin items. add_pin, remove_pin and commit_pins push SetLinkPinsCommand, set_pins only shows pins, pin_color is the color of the pins. GraphicsStage.find_link_at editor/graphics/graphics_stage.py Finds the link near a scene position, with a tolerance, so a thin link can be double-clicked. StageGraphView.mouseDoubleClickEvent editor/views/stage_graph_view.py Adds a pin on a double-clicked link. A double-clicked pin removes itself.

Things that are easy to get wrong:

  • The scene is rebuilt after every command. GraphicsStage.rebuild_current_scope runs on every change of the undo stack, so the GraphicsLink and its pins are new items after a command. Don't keep a reference to a link or pin item across a push, and don't touch an item after the command that deletes it (GraphicsLinkPin clears its state before committing for this reason).
  • Dragging doesn't push. A pin only moves the item while it is dragged and the move is pushed once, on release, so one drag is one undo step.
  • Don't take the pin color from the pen. A link between plugs of different colors is stroked with a gradient, and the color of a gradient pen is black. Use GraphicsLink.pin_color.
  • Graphics objects passed to create_graphics_object for a link get pins= as a keyword argument next to link_uuid. A replacement for GraphicsLink registered under core.link (see graphics objects) has to accept it, which is easiest by subclassing GraphicsLink.

docs.title: Tests and images
docs.text:
The tests are in tests/editor/test_link_pins.py: path building, serialization, the command with undo, deserialization from a file, and the mouse interactions on a real view.

The images on this page and in the user guide are rendered, not screenshots. Regenerate them after changing how links or pins are drawn:

uv run python scripts/docs_images.py links    # docs/_static/images/link-pins/

docs.title: Profiling
docs.text:
Nyx has a small profiling helper in nyx.utils.profiling. It combines two things:

  • a timer that is always on and cheap: the decorated function logs how long it took,
  • a call profiler (cProfile) that is only on when asked for, and writes a file you can inspect with snakeviz.

docs.title: The decorator
docs.text:
from nyx.utils.profiling import profile

@profile()
def rebuild_everything():
    ...

@profile(name="Stages imported", text="{name} in {seconds:.4f}s")
def import_stages(paths):
    ...
Argument Meaning name Label used in the message and available as {name}. Defaults to the function name. text Format of the log message, with {name} and {seconds}. Defaults to "{name}: {seconds:.4f}s".

The timing message is written at INFO level by the NyxProfiler logger, on every call, with or without profiling. The decorator is applied to loading plugins (NyxPluginLoader.load_plugins_from_paths), initializing them (NyxPluginManager.initialize_plugins) and importing stages in the editor (editor/utils/io.py), so the log of every start shows what they cost.

docs.title: Turning the call profiler on
docs.text:
Set NYX_PROFILING to a number other than 0 (use 1). The value is read as an integer when Nyx is imported, so words such as true are not accepted.

NYX_PROFILING=1 nyx
NYX_PROFILING=1 nyx stage run path/to/stage.nyx

Each decorated call then runs under cProfile, and its statistics are saved to

<user directory>/profiling/<function name>_profile.pstats

(see Customization for the user directory). The log prints the snakeviz "<file>" command to open it. A later call of the same function overwrites the file.

Nested decorated calls in the same thread are not profiled twice: the outermost call owns the profiler, and inner functions are only timed.

docs.title: Viewing the results
docs.text:
make pstats                       # opens the profiling folder with snakeviz
snakeviz ~/.config/nyx/profiling/initialize_plugins_profile.pstats
python -m pstats ~/.config/nyx/profiling/initialize_plugins_profile.pstats

make pstats and the log hint call snakeviz, which is not a dependency of the project. Install it into your environment (uv tool install snakeviz, or pip install snakeviz).

docs.title: Profiling something new
docs.text:
1. Decorate the function with @profile().
  2. Run with NYX_PROFILING=1, do the operation, and open the .pstats file.
  3. Remove the decorator again if the function is a hot path: the timer is cheap, but it logs at INFO on every call.

To profile a whole stage run without editing any code, use cProfile directly:

uv run python -m cProfile -o run.pstats -m nyx stage run stage.nyx

docs.title: Other tools for finding slowness
docs.text:
• NYX_DEBUG=1 logs at debug level. Every executed node logs its path and how long it took (Executed in 0.0123: /stage/loop/log).
  • The config option editor_widgets.graphics_stage.viewport_debug_overlay (also an action in the editor) draws performance numbers over the graph view.
  • editor_widgets.graphics_stage.nodes.hover_diagnostics shows the model roles as a tooltip, useful when a value looks wrong.

docs.title: The registry
docs.text:
NYX_REGISTRY is the single place where Nyx keeps everything plugins provide. When a stage file says a node has type_id: "core:branch", the registry is what turns that string into a class. It is a module-level instance of NyxRegistry:

from nyx.api.v1 import NYX_REGISTRY

docs.title: What it holds
docs.text:
Attribute Content Key plugins NyxPluginRegistryEntry per discovered plugin: the class, whether it is enabled, and the initialized instance plugin type id nodes node classes node type id node_components component classes component type id datatypes Datatype instances datatype type id util_objects util object classes util object type id graphics_objects graphics item classes, the built-in ones included graphics object id qml_import_root_directories directories QML modules are imported from n/a

All keys are plain strings with a namespace, "<namespace>:<name>" (core:value, function:math.add), and must be unique inside their category. A duplicate is logged as an error and skipped: the first registration wins.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Content gets into the registry in three steps. They run in this order at application startup (NyxApplication.__init__, between pre_initialize and post_initialize).

docs.title: 1. Discovery and registration of plugin classes
docs.text:
NyxPluginLoader finds nyx_plugin.py files and imports them. Importing is enough to register the plugin class: the @NyxPluginManager.register_plugin() decorator validates it (it must have a type_id, and the id must be new) and adds a NyxPluginRegistryEntry to NYX_REGISTRY.plugins through add_plugin. A plugin that fails validation is logged and left out; the others continue.

The loader searches, in this order:

  1. the directory of nyx.stdlib,
  2. nyx/plugins,
  3. the plugin_paths config value,
  4. the NYX_PLUGIN_PATH environment variable.

Plugin files inside the nyx package are imported by their real module name (so from nyx.stdlib.nodes.value import ... in another plugin gets the same class the registry holds). Files outside of it are loaded with their folder registered as a package, so relative imports (from . import operations) work.

docs.title: 2. Initialization
docs.text: NyxPluginManager.initialize_plugins() calls initialize() on each enabled entry that has no instance yet. The plugin builds its contents (NyxPluginContents) and the entry keeps the instance. Passing include=[...] enables exactly the listed plugins (this is what the with_plugins test marker does).

docs.title: 3. Registering the contents
docs.text:
NYX_REGISTRY.register_plugin_content() rebuilds everything from the initialized, enabled plugins:

  1. clear nodes, node_components, datatypes, util_objects, and reset graphics_objects to the built-in ones,
  2. register the core datatypes (core_types.CORE_DATATYPES),
  3. for each plugin entry, in discovery order: node components, nodes, datatypes, util objects, graphics objects and its QML import root.

Registering a node, component or util object class also sets SOURCE_PLUGIN on it to the plugin entry. Serialization writes the plugin id as source_plugin into the file, and the QML resolver uses the plugin's QML_MODULE_NAME to find a component's editor. Because the core plugin is discovered first, its ids can't be overridden by another plugin.

Note

Step 3 starts by clearing, so registry content isn't additive across calls: it is always the contents of the currently enabled plugins. Don't add classes to the registry's dictionaries directly.

docs.title: Lookups
docs.text:
Method Returns get_node_cls(type_id) the node class. Logs an error and returns None when unknown. get_node_component_cls(type_id) the component class, or None. get_util_object_cls(type_id) the util object class. Logs an error and returns None when unknown. get_graphics_object_cls(type_id) the graphics item class, or None. get_datatype(type_id) the Datatype, or None. resolve_datatype(type_id) the Datatype, falling back to OBJECT_DATATYPE for a missing or unknown id (logged). Use this when reading files. infer_datatype(value) first registered datatype whose Python type is exactly type(value), else Object. find_datatype_for_type(python_type) datatype claiming that Python type, or None. Used for the type hints of function nodes. iter_datatypes(), iter_node_components(), iter_plugins() iterate the registered content. resolve_qml_source(module_uri, type_name) path of <root>/<module/path>/<type_name>.qml in the first import root that has it, else FileNotFoundError. register_builtin_graphics_object(type_id, cls) for the editor: graphics items that exist whatever plugins are enabled (nodes, plugs, links).

infer_datatype and find_datatype_for_type return the first match in registration order, so two datatypes with the same Python type resolve to the one registered earlier.

docs.title: QML import roots
docs.text: The registry also keeps the list of QML import roots: the editor's own qml folder first, then the qml folder next to each enabled plugin file (NyxPlugin.qml_directory()) as it registers. NyxEditorApplication hands the list to the QML engine (sync_qml_import_paths). See A QML editor for a component.

docs.title: Using the registry from your code
docs.text:
from nyx.api.v1 import NYX_REGISTRY

for type_id, node_cls in NYX_REGISTRY.nodes.items():
    print(type_id, node_cls.get_type_display_name(), sorted(node_cls.get_tags()))

NYX_REGISTRY.get_node_cls("core:branch")
NYX_REGISTRY.get_datatype("core:int").accepts(NYX_REGISTRY.get_datatype("core:float"))

NYX_REGISTRY.clear() empties everything. It exists for tests.

docs.title: Writing plugins
docs.text:
Everything that a stage can contain comes from a plugin, including the content that ships with Nyx. This section shows how to add each kind of content:

I want to add Page A new kind of node New node A node that calls a Python function New function node A new kind of component (a plug on a node) New component A custom editor for a component in the UI New QML for a component A new datatype New datatype A note-like object that doesn't execute New util object A custom drawing for a util object New graphics object

Import from nyx.api.v1 only. It is the public, versioned API; nyx.core and nyx.editor can change without notice. Look at nyx/stdlib (the core plugin) and nyx/plugins/functions/* for working examples of everything below.

docs.title: Anatomy of a plugin
docs.text:
A plugin is a folder containing a nyx_plugin.py. The file defines one subclass of NyxPlugin and registers it with a decorator.

my_plugins/                      <- put this folder in plugin_paths or NYX_PLUGIN_PATH
└── studio_tools/
    ├── nyx_plugin.py            <- found by the loader (any depth below the path)
    ├── nodes/
    │   └── greeter.py
    ├── components/
    │   └── color.py
    ├── qml/                     <- QML import root of the plugin
    │   └── StudioTools/         <- QML module, named by QML_MODULE_NAME
    │       ├── qmldir
    │       └── ColorComponentItem.qml
    └── resources/
        └── icons/

# studio_tools/nyx_plugin.py
import typing

from nyx.api.v1 import NyxPlugin, NyxPluginManager

from .nodes.greeter import GreeterNode
from .components.color import ColorComponent


@NyxPluginManager.register_plugin()
class StudioTools(NyxPlugin):
    """Tools of the studio."""

    QML_MODULE_NAME = "StudioTools"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        """str: unique plugin id."""
        return "StudioTools"

    @classmethod
    def get_palette_name(cls) -> str:
        """str: name of the section of the palette holding the types of the plugin."""
        return "Studio"

    @classmethod
    def initialize(cls) -> typing.Self:
        """Create the plugin and list its content.

        Returns:
            typing.Self: initialized plugin.
        """
        plugin = cls()
        plugin.contents.node_components = [ColorComponent]
        plugin.contents.nodes = [GreeterNode]
        return plugin

The pieces:

  • @NyxPluginManager.register_plugin() registers the class when the file is imported. A plugin with no get_type_id, or with an id that is already taken, is logged and skipped.
  • get_type_id() is the unique id of the plugin. It is stored in saved stages (source_plugin), so don't change it once stages exist.
  • get_type_display_name() (defaults to the id) and get_palette_name() (defaults to the display name) are used by the UI. get_tags() can return a set of tags.
  • initialize() is called once at startup. Create the plugin and fill plugin.contents (NyxPluginContents):
Field Holds nodes node classes node_components component classes datatypes Datatype instances util_objects util object classes graphics_objects graphics item classes (QGraphicsItem subclasses with a get_type_id) register_function_node(func) method that generates a node class from a function and adds it to nodes register_function_module(module, namespace) the same for every public function of a module
  • QML_MODULE_NAME is the name of the QML module in the plugin's qml folder, needed only when a component has a custom QML editor.

The plugin class also helps locating files next to it: root_directory(), qml_directory(), resources_directory(), icons_directory() and get_icon(name).

docs.title: Where plugins are found
docs.text:
NyxPluginLoader searches recursively for nyx_plugin.py in nyx.stdlib, the built-in nyx/plugins, every directory in the plugin_paths config value, and every directory in the NYX_PLUGIN_PATH environment variable. See The registry for what happens next.

NYX_PLUGIN_PATH=/studio/nyx_plugins nyx
NYX_PLUGIN_PATH=/studio/nyx_plugins nyx stage run nightly.nyx

Because the plugin file is loaded as part of a package named after its folder, use relative imports between your files (from .nodes.greeter import GreeterNode), and keep the folder name unique among your plugins.

docs.title: Type ids
docs.text:
Every node, component, datatype, util object and graphics object has a type id: a string stored in saved stages. Rules to follow:

  • Use namespace:name, with a namespace of your own (studio:greeter). core: and function: are taken.
  • They have to be unique per category; a duplicate is logged and the first one wins.
  • They are part of your file format. Renaming one breaks stages that use it.

docs.title: Icons
docs.text: get_type_icon() returns a Qt resource path such as :/icons/function. The built-in icons (:/icons/..., :/core/icons/...) are available to every plugin. To ship your own, add a .qrc file, compile it with pyside6-rcc and import the generated module from your nyx_plugin.py (the stdlib does from .resources import resources_rc). Use a unique prefix in the .qrc so paths don't clash.

docs.title: Testing a plugin
docs.text:
The repository's test suite shows the pattern. tests/conftest.py starts the application offscreen, and the with_plugins marker initializes the plugins named in it:

import pytest

from nyx.api.v1 import Stage, commands

@pytest.mark.with_plugins("NyxStdlib", "StudioTools")
def test_greeter(nyx_app):
    stage = Stage()  # keep the reference: commands hold their stage weakly
    command = commands.CreateNodeCommand(stage=stage, type_id="studio:greeter")
    stage.push_command(command)
    greeter = command.result_node

    stage.crawler.start(greeter)
    assert greeter.greeting_cpnt.pull_value() == "Hello, World."

Make sure your plugin folder is on NYX_PLUGIN_PATH when the tests run so the loader finds it. Every change to a stage goes through a command (push_command), which is also what the editor does, so undo works for it. tests/stage_helpers.py has small helpers that wrap this.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] nyx_plugin.py registers exactly one NyxPlugin subclass, with a unique id.
  • [ ] Type ids have your namespace.
  • [ ] Imports come from nyx.api.v1.
  • [ ] Every class has get_type_id, get_type_display_name and a get_description.
  • [ ] Nodes work when their stage is saved and loaded again, see New node.
  • [ ] Google-style docstrings (Args:, Returns:, Raises:), they become the descriptions in the UI for function nodes.

docs.title: New QML for a component
docs.text: The inspector and the nodes of the editor show components with small QML items. A component type without its own item uses a generic one (NodeComponentItem.qml). To give a type a custom editor, put a QML file in your plugin and name it in EDITOR_QML.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
studio_tools/
├── nyx_plugin.py                  QML_MODULE_NAME = "StudioTools"
└── qml/                           <- NyxPlugin.qml_directory(), an import root
    └── StudioTools/               <- the module, same name as QML_MODULE_NAME
        ├── qmldir
        └── ColorComponentItem.qml

// qml/StudioTools/qmldir
module StudioTools

ColorComponentItem 1.0 ColorComponentItem.qml

class ColorComponent(NodeComponent):
    EDITOR_QML = "ColorComponentItem"     # file name without .qml

class StudioTools(NyxPlugin):
    QML_MODULE_NAME = "StudioTools"       # folder inside qml/

How it is found: when a component needs its editor, Nyx asks the registry for <import root>/StudioTools/ColorComponentItem.qml (NYX_REGISTRY.resolve_qml_source), searching the registered import roots. The qml folder of every enabled plugin is an import root, the editor's own qml folder is one too. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError with the roots it tried.

The file is loaded by its path, as an item inside the component's row in the inspector and on the node, and only while the component is expanded. The qmldir makes the type importable by name (import StudioTools) for other QML files and for the QML language server; keep it up to date like the stdlib does. If loading fails, the log shows Editor failed to load: <file>.

The QML engine of the editor knows the import roots, so your files can import NyxEditor.Common for the shared building blocks.

docs.title: The easy way: derive from ComponentValue
docs.text:
ComponentValue (from NyxEditor.Common) holds the editing logic of a value: the component, the editing state, the masks of the value, and what happens when the user finishes typing. You only provide what is shown with delegates.

// qml/StudioTools/ColorComponentItem.qml
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import NyxEditor.Common

ComponentValue {
    id: colorItemRoot

    label: "Color:"
    // The text is a color, keep it as typed instead of evaluating it as an expression.
    evaluateOnFinish: false

    // Shown when not editing
    displayDelegate: Row {
        spacing: 6

        Rectangle {
            width: 18
            height: 18
            radius: 3
            border.color: palette.mid
            color: colorItemRoot.maskedText
        }

        Label {
            text: colorItemRoot.maskedText
            opacity: colorItemRoot.editable ? 1.0 : 0.6

            TapHandler {
                onDoubleTapped: colorItemRoot.requestEdit()
            }
        }
    }

    // Shown while editing the raw value
    editDelegate: TextField {
        // Set once: what is typed must not be replaced by a binding.
        Component.onCompleted: {
            text = colorItemRoot.textOf(ComponentValue.Raw);
            forceActiveFocus();
            selectAll();
        }
        onAccepted: if (colorItemRoot.editing)
            colorItemRoot.finishEdit(text)
        onActiveFocusChanged: if (!activeFocus && colorItemRoot.editing)
            colorItemRoot.finishEdit(text)
        Keys.onEscapePressed: colorItemRoot.cancelEdit()
    }

    // Children are placed after the delegate
    EditButton {
        editor: colorItemRoot
    }
}

docs.title: What ComponentValue gives you
docs.text:
Member Meaning component The component being edited (model row): component.rawValue, .cachedValue, .displayValue, .isEditable, .inputLinks, .datatypeId, ... controller The components controller; controller.setComponentValue(...) is what finishEdit ends up calling. Controllers can offer more, for instance selectFile that the File item uses. label Text before the value. editable Whether editing is allowed. Defaults to component.isEditable; bind it to && !hasInputConnection to forbid editing a linked value (the Value item does). editing In edit mode. evaluateOnFinish true: the typed text is evaluated as a Python expression when set. false: it is stored as typed. displayDelegate, editDelegate, cachedDelegate The Components shown for each state, see the rules below. restingMask Value shown when not editing: ComponentValue.Display (default), Raw or Cached. maskedText The text of the current mask. textOf(mask) reads any of them. requestEdit(), beginEdit(), finishEdit(text), cancelEdit() Drive the edit state. finishEdit sends the new text to the component unless it didn't change. field The item the current delegate created. default property alias content Items declared inside ComponentValue are placed after the delegate.

Which delegate shows: editing selects editDelegate; otherwise a Cached mask uses cachedDelegate (falling back to displayDelegate) and any other mask uses displayDelegate.

Ready-made building blocks in NyxEditor.Common: EditButton (edit/confirm button following editor.editing), DatatypeSelector (pick the datatype of a component), and CollapsibleFrame, DescriptionToolTip, TagsList and others used by the palettes. Read editor/qml/NyxEditor/Common and the items in stdlib/qml/NyxStdlib (ValueComponentItem, FileComponentItem, CommentComponentItem, FlowComponentItem) as examples. The Comment item renders Markdown, the File item adds a file dialog button.

docs.title: A freer editor
docs.text: If ComponentValue doesn't fit, your root item can be any Item. It must declare property var component, which the editor binds to the model row of the component, and can reach the components controller like ComponentValue does (root.componentsController). Keep the item small: one is created for every expanded component on screen.

docs.title: Checking it
docs.text:
1. make qrc is not needed for QML files in a plugin folder; they are read from disk. It is needed if your QML refers to icons from a .qrc you changed.
  2. Start the editor with your plugin on NYX_PLUGIN_PATH, add the component to a node, expand it and look at the log. A QML error is printed there with the file and line.
  3. In the repository, generate_qmlls_config.py writes the config the QML language server needs to resolve the NyxEditor.* imports while you edit.

docs.title: New component
docs.text: A component is a plug on a node: it holds a value, can be linked, and can run something when its node executes. Add a new component type when several nodes need the same kind of plug with its own behavior or editor. For a value that only needs another datatype, use a Value component with that datatype instead (New datatype).

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
A component that holds a color as #RRGGBB text and complains about anything else:

# studio_tools/components/color.py
import re

from nyx.api.v1 import (
    NodeComponent,
    CoreNodeComponents,
    CoreDatatypes,
    NodeComponentFlag,
)

HEX_COLOR = re.compile(r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}")


class ColorComponent(NodeComponent):
    """Component holding a color as #RRGGBB."""

    DEFAULT_NAME = "color"
    EDITOR_QML = "ColorComponentItem"   # see "New QML for a component"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        """str: component type id."""
        return "studio:color"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_display_name(cls) -> str:
        """str: name shown in the UI."""
        return "Color"

    @classmethod
    def get_description(cls) -> str:
        """str: what the component type does, shown in the palette."""
        return "Holds a color as #RRGGBB."

    @classmethod
    def get_tags(cls) -> set[str]:
        """set[str]: component tags."""
        return {"value"}

    @classmethod
    def get_type_default_value(cls) -> str:
        """str: initial value of new components."""
        return "#ffffff"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_default_datatype(cls) -> str:
        """str: the color is kept as text."""
        return CoreDatatypes.STRING

    @classmethod
    def get_type_default_flags(cls) -> NodeComponentFlag:
        """NodeComponentFlag: flags new components start with."""
        return NodeComponentFlag.EDITABLE | NodeComponentFlag.LITERAL

    @classmethod
    def get_type_enforced_flags(cls) -> NodeComponentFlag:
        """NodeComponentFlag: always literal, text is never evaluated as an expression."""
        return NodeComponentFlag.LITERAL

    def evaluate(self):
        """Mark the component as invalid when the value isn't a color."""
        value = self.pull_value()
        self.invalid_reason = (
            "" if isinstance(value, str) and HEX_COLOR.fullmatch(value) else
            f"Not a #RRGGBB color: {value!r}"
        )

Register it with plugin.contents.node_components = [ColorComponent], and use it from a node with self.components_model.create_component("studio:color"). Users can also add it to any node from the editor (the "add component" palette lists every registered component type).

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text: Attribute Purpose DEFAULT_NAME Address name new components start with. EDITOR_QML Name of the QML file that edits the component, without extension, see New QML for a component. Left empty the generic item is used. VALUE_STORAGE_CLS ValueStorage subclass that decides how the value is set, evaluated, cast and displayed. Override it to change evaluation (for instance never eval, or parse your own syntax).

docs.title: Class methods (the type)
docs.text: Method Purpose get_type_id() Unique id stored in files, namespace:name. get_type_display_name() Name in the UI. Defaults to the class name. get_type_icon() Resource path of the icon. get_description(), get_tags() Palette text and search tags. get_type_default_value() Initial value. get_type_default_datatype() Datatype id new components are hinted with. Default core:object. get_type_default_flags() NodeComponentFlag set on new components. get_type_enforced_flags() Flags every component of the type has, also when an old file is loaded. Use for rules of the type. get_default_expanded_state() Whether new components start expanded in the node. get_link_width_multiplier() Thickness of the links coming from the component. get_graphics_object_id() Id of the graphics item drawing the plug. Defaults to the standard plug.

docs.title: Instance hooks
docs.text:
Method Called evaluate() While the node evaluates its components, after the value was evaluated and cast. execute() While the node executes its components. Not called for static or inactive components. Script components run their file here. evaluation_hook(), execution_hook() The wrappers that clear the cache, skip inactive and static components, and call the two above. Override only to change those rules.

Everything in the node properties table applies to components: readable, writable, is_editable, is_literal, is_static, set_datatype, pull_value, push_value.

docs.title: Behavior to know about
docs.text:
• The value is one of three: raw (as set), cached (evaluated) and display (text). Read with pull_value(), which follows links; raw_value and cached_value read this component's own.
  • invalid_reason marks a component as not usable and shows the reason in the UI. It is not saved. Set it back to "" when the problem is gone.
  • Flags that are static (like File, which sets STATIC | EDITABLE) are skipped when the node executes its components: the value is only data.
  • Serialization: type id, name, value, default value, datatype, flags and note are saved. Override serialize_value / deserialize_value when the value isn't plain JSON (a Python object, a set, a class).
  • The plugin owns the type: a stage saved with your component can only be opened with your plugin loaded. Keep the type id stable.

docs.title: Adding a component to a node in code
docs.text:
component = self.components_model.create_component("studio:color")
component.name = "tint"
component.writable = True
self.components_model.add_component(component)

Or from a command: commands.AddNodeComponentCommand(...), which supports undo.

docs.title: New datatype
docs.text: A datatype tells Nyx what kind of value a component holds: how the plug is drawn, which components it can link to, and how a value is converted. A datatype is data, not a class: an instance of the frozen dataclass Datatype.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
# studio_tools/datatypes.py
from nyx.api.v1 import Datatype, GraphicsPlugShape


def cast_to_vector3(value) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Convert a sequence of three numbers.

    Args:
        value: Anything that can be iterated for three numbers.

    Raises:
        ValueError: There aren't three values.

    Returns:
        The vector.
    """
    x, y, z = (float(each) for each in value)
    return (x, y, z)


VECTOR3 = Datatype(
    type_id="studio:vector3",
    display_name="Vector3",
    color="#FF8A5B",
    caster=cast_to_vector3,
    python_type=tuple,
    plug_shape=GraphicsPlugShape.TRIANGLE,
    default_factory=lambda: (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
)

Register it in initialize and use it in a node:

plugin.contents.datatypes = [VECTOR3]

# in a node's setup()
self.position_cpnt.set_datatype("studio:vector3")

A value component with that datatype now shows an orange triangle plug, starts at (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), and anything pulled into it through a link is cast with cast_to_vector3.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning type_id Unique id, namespace:name. Stored in stage files. display_name Name in the UI (the datatype selector). color Plug color as hex. caster Function that converts an evaluated value. Must raise when it can't; Nyx wraps the error in a DatatypeCastError. Defaults to returning the value as it is. python_type Exact Python type of the values. Used to infer the datatype of a value and to choose the datatype for a type hint of a function node. Leave None if there isn't one. plug_shape GraphicsPlugShape: CIRCLE, TRIANGLE, PENTAGON, SQUARE, SQUARE_MATRIX, BARS, DIAMOND. Circles are the default, pick another shape to tell types apart without color. default_factory Creates the starting value. Called for every new value, so mutable defaults aren't shared. Default gives None. is_wildcard Links to every datatype (but ones that ignore wildcards). ignores_wildcards Links only to itself and what compatible_with lists. Flow uses it. compatible_with frozenset of type ids it can link to besides itself. Declare it on both datatypes if the compatibility goes both ways, as Integer and Float do. selectable False hides it from the datatype selector. For datatypes that belong to one component type.

The behavior, in detail:

  • accepts(other) is what decides if a link is allowed: same id, or listed in compatible_with, then wildcards (unless one side ignores them), see Datatypes.
  • cast(value) runs the caster and raises DatatypeCastError with a message including the value and the reason.
  • matches(value) is true only for the exact type (type(value) is python_type), so a bool doesn't count as an int.

docs.title: Design advice
docs.text:
• Be strict in the caster, loose in compatible_with. The caster should refuse what it can't understand. The warning that follows names the component and the reason.
  • One Python type, one datatype. infer_datatype and function node hints pick the first registered datatype for a Python type. If two plugins claim tuple, the one registered first wins. Use a distinct python_type (a small class) if your values need to be told apart.
  • Avoid wildcards. Wildcards make links between unrelated things possible, which hides mistakes. Use compatible_with to name the few types you really want to interoperate with.
  • The value is saved as JSON. A component writes its value to the stage file as JSON, so a tuple becomes a list there. Make the caster accept the shapes JSON gives (lists, dicts, strings, numbers). If the value is something else, the component type needs serialize_value and deserialize_value.
  • An unknown datatype becomes Object. A stage saved with your datatype and opened without the plugin warns Unknown datatype ... and falls back to Object.

docs.title: Using a datatype in components
docs.text:
• In setup() of a node: component.set_datatype("studio:vector3").
  • For a new component type: return the id from get_type_default_datatype(), see New component.
  • In functions: annotate parameters with the Python type (def move(offset: tuple): ...). See New function node.

docs.title: New function node
docs.text: The quickest way to add a node: write a normal Python function and register it. Nyx generates a node class for it (a FunctionNode subclass) with a flow component, one value component per parameter and a return component.

docs.title: One function
docs.text:
# studio_tools/nyx_plugin.py
import typing

from nyx.api.v1 import NyxPlugin, NyxPluginManager


def clamp(value: float, low: float = 0.0, high: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """Limit a number to a range.

    Args:
        value: The number to limit.
        low: Smallest result.
        high: Largest result.

    Returns:
        The number, not below low and not above high.
    """
    return max(low, min(high, value))


@NyxPluginManager.register_plugin()
class StudioFunctions(NyxPlugin):
    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        return "StudioFunctions"

    @classmethod
    def get_palette_name(cls) -> str:
        return "Studio Functions"

    @classmethod
    def initialize(cls) -> typing.Self:
        plugin = cls()
        plugin.contents.register_function_node(
            clamp, type_id="function:studio.clamp", tags=["math"]
        )
        return plugin

register_function_node(func, type_id=None, tags=()):

Argument Meaning func A named function. Lambdas and other callables without a name raise TypeError. type_id Node type id. Defaults to function:<module>.<qualified name>, which depends on where the function is defined: give an explicit id to keep saved stages working when you move code. tags Tags besides the automatic function tag.

It returns the generated node class and raises ValueError if the plugin already registered a node with that type id.

docs.title: A whole module
docs.text:
register_function_module(module, namespace) registers every public function of a module, as function:<namespace>.<function name>, tagged with the namespace. This is how the built-in plugins are written (nyx/plugins/functions/math_operations):

# math_operations/nyx_plugin.py
from . import operations

plugin.contents.register_function_module(operations, namespace="math")

Public means: defined in that module (not imported into it) and not starting with an underscore. Put helpers in other modules or prefix them with _.

docs.title: What is generated
docs.text:
From the function Becomes Name The default node name, and the display name with underscores replaced by spaces and capitalized (floor_divide becomes "Floor Divide"). Type hints of the parameters The datatype of each parameter component, see below. Default values The default and the initial value of the parameter component. First paragraph of the docstring The node description in the palette. Args: section The tooltips of the parameter components. Returns: section (or the first line of the docstring) The tooltip of the return component. Return type hint The datatype of the return component.

*args and **kwargs are skipped (with a warning in the log). Positional-only parameters are passed positionally, the others by keyword.

docs.title: Type hints choose the datatypes
docs.text: The hint is looked up in the registry (find_datatype_for_type): X | None counts as X, a generic like list[int] as list, and the first datatype registered for exactly that Python type wins. No hint, or a type no datatype claims, gives Object, which links to anything. Register your own datatype (New datatype) with a python_type to have functions that use that type get properly colored plugs.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text:
The node is a flow node. When it executes it pulls every parameter, calls the function and stores the result in return without evaluating it (so a string result isn't run as an expression). An exception from the function fails the node like any other.

Values are cast to the datatype of the parameter component (see Datatypes).

docs.title: When a function is not enough
docs.text: If you need more than the generated shape, for instance flow outputs, a scope or per-run state, write a node by hand.

docs.title: New graphics object
docs.text:
A graphics object is the QGraphicsItem that draws something of a stage in the graph view. Nyx keeps the model (nodes, components, links, util objects) apart from how it is drawn, and joins them by an id:

stage object type                         graphics object
   get_graphics_object_id()  ──id──▶  NYX_REGISTRY.graphics_objects[id]  ──▶  item

The editor builds the item with create_graphics_object(stage_object, ...): it reads type(stage_object).get_graphics_object_id(), finds the class in the registry and calls it. A type that returns None isn't drawn; an id with no registered class logs Unknown graphics object ....

Id Drawn by Registered by core.node (CoreGraphicsObjects.NODE) GraphicsNode the editor, always core.plug (PLUG) GraphicsPlug the editor, always core.link (LINK) GraphicsLink the editor, always core.note (NOTE) GraphicsNote the NyxStdlib plugin core.group (GROUP) GraphicsGroup the NyxStdlib plugin

Most plugins never write one: nodes and components use the standard node and plug items, and are customized through their data (names, datatypes, plug shapes, QML editors). Write a graphics object for a new util object.

Warning

Graphics objects belong to the editor (nyx.editor), which is not part of nyx.api.v1 and isn't versioned like it. The base class lives in nyx.editor.graphics.graphics_util_object. The standard library does the same (nyx/stdlib/graphics_objects), use it as the reference and expect to adjust when the editor internals change.

docs.title: A complete example: the checklist
docs.text:
# studio_tools/graphics_objects/checklist.py
from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets

from nyx.editor.graphics.graphics_util_object import GraphicsUtilObject
from nyx.editor.graphics.level_of_detail import LevelOfDetail


class GraphicsChecklist(GraphicsUtilObject):
    """Draws a ChecklistObject as a card with its items."""

    RADIUS = 6.0
    PADDING = 8.0
    Z_VALUE = 0.4        # below nodes, notes are at 0.5

    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        """str: id the graphics object is registered with."""
        return "studio.checklist"

    def paint(
        self,
        painter: QtGui.QPainter,
        option: QtWidgets.QStyleOptionGraphicsItem,
        widget: QtWidgets.QWidget | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Draw the card and its items.

        Args:
            painter (QtGui.QPainter): painter.
            option (QtWidgets.QStyleOptionGraphicsItem): style options.
            widget (QtWidgets.QWidget | None): painted widget.
        """
        lod = LevelOfDetail.from_painter(painter, text_size=10.0)
        rect = QtCore.QRectF(QtCore.QPointF(), self.item_size)
        painter.setPen(QtGui.QPen(self.color.darker(160), 1.0))
        painter.setBrush(self.color)
        painter.drawRoundedRect(rect, self.RADIUS, self.RADIUS)
        if lod.shows_text:
            painter.setPen(QtGui.QColor("#202020"))
            text = "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in self.util_object.items)
            painter.drawText(
                rect.adjusted(self.PADDING, self.PADDING, -self.PADDING, -self.PADDING),
                int(QtCore.Qt.AlignLeft | QtCore.Qt.AlignTop | QtCore.Qt.TextWordWrap),
                text,
            )
        self.paint_selection(painter, self.RADIUS)

    def edit(self) -> None:
        """Ask for the items, one per line."""
        text, accepted = QtWidgets.QInputDialog.getMultiLineText(
            self.parent_widget(), "Checklist", "Items:", "\n".join(self.util_object.items)
        )
        if accepted:
            self.push_properties({"items": text.splitlines()}, "Edit checklist")

The util object returns this id from get_graphics_object_id() ("studio.checklist" in New util object), and the plugin lists the class:

plugin.contents.util_objects = [ChecklistObject]
plugin.contents.graphics_objects = [GraphicsChecklist]

color reads a color attribute of the util object; the example has none, so it draws gray. Add a color property (serialized like the note's) for color presets and the color menu.

docs.title: What GraphicsUtilObject does for you
docs.text:
Member Purpose __init__(util_object, parent=None) Called by the factory. The item is selectable, takes hover events and calls refresh. util_object, uuid The model object and its id. refresh() Re-reads size and position from the model, and updates the item. Called when the model changed (undo, redo, paste). Override and call super() when you cache anything. item_size, color, is_editable Current size (follows the mouse while resizing), color and whether the object isn't locked. paint(...) You implement it. Draw into QRectF(QPointF(), item_size). paint_selection(painter, radius) Draws the selection outline and the resize grip. Call it last. edit() Called on double click. Implement it to edit the content. push_properties(properties, text) Pushes a SetUtilObjectPropertiesCommand, so the change is undoable. Never change the util object directly. set_color(color) Pushes a color change. parent_widget() A widget to parent dialogs to. Z_VALUE, COLOR_PRESETS, HANDLE_SIZE Class attributes to tune.

Moving and resizing with the mouse is built in: they push commands that set position and size, and objects in a locked scope (the contents of a reference) can't be moved.

docs.title: Level of detail
docs.text: LevelOfDetail.from_painter(painter, text_size=..., shape_size=...) tells how much is worth drawing at the current zoom: MINIMAL (a flat placeholder), NO_TEXT (shapes only) or FULL. Check lod.shows_text and lod.shows_shapes before expensive drawing, so big graphs stay fast when zoomed out.

docs.title: Registering
docs.text:
• NyxPluginContents.graphics_objects takes classes with a get_type_id classmethod. The registry skips (and logs) an id that is already registered.
  • Graphics objects are registered when the plugin content is, so they are available when the editor builds its first scene.
  • Built-in ids are kept when the registry is rebuilt; plugin ones are dropped and registered again from the enabled plugins.

docs.title: Drawing nodes, plugs or links differently
docs.text: Node and component types return an id from get_graphics_object_id() too (core.node and core.plug by default), so a type can point at a different registered item. The standard items are GraphicsNode, GraphicsPlug and GraphicsLink in nyx.editor.graphics. They are tied closely to the scene, so subclass them and override small pieces instead of writing an item from scratch. This isn't used by any plugin in the repository yet.

docs.title: New node
docs.text: A node is a Node subclass that creates its components in setup and does its work in evaluate and execute.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
# studio_tools/nodes/greeter.py
from nyx.api.v1 import Node, CoreNodeComponents, CoreDatatypes


class GreeterNode(Node):
    """Flow node that builds a greeting for a name."""

    DEFAULT_NAME = "greeter"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        """str: node type id."""
        return "studio:greeter"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_display_name(cls) -> str:
        """str: name shown in the UI."""
        return "Greeter"

    @classmethod
    def get_description(cls) -> str:
        """str: what the node type does, shown in the palette."""
        return "Builds a greeting for the given name."

    @classmethod
    def get_tags(cls) -> set[str]:
        """set[str]: node tags, used to find the node in the palette."""
        return {"common", "text"}

    def setup(self):
        """Add the flow, the name input and the greeting output."""
        self.flow_cpnt = self.components_model.create_component(CoreNodeComponents.FLOW)
        self.flow_cpnt.name = "flow"
        self.flow_cpnt.readable = True   # output: the flow can leave through it
        self.flow_cpnt.writable = True   # input: the flow can enter through it

        self.who_cpnt = self.components_model.create_component(CoreNodeComponents.VALUE)
        self.who_cpnt.name = "who"
        self.who_cpnt.description = "Who to greet."
        self.who_cpnt.writable = True        # can be linked to
        self.who_cpnt.is_editable = True     # can be typed in the UI
        self.who_cpnt.is_literal = True      # text is kept as typed, not evaluated
        self.who_cpnt.set_datatype(CoreDatatypes.STRING)
        self.who_cpnt.push_value("World")

        self.greeting_cpnt = self.components_model.create_component(
            CoreNodeComponents.VALUE
        )
        self.greeting_cpnt.name = "greeting"
        self.greeting_cpnt.description = "The greeting."
        self.greeting_cpnt.readable = True   # can be the source of links
        self.greeting_cpnt.is_editable = False
        self.greeting_cpnt.set_datatype(CoreDatatypes.STRING)

        for component in (self.flow_cpnt, self.who_cpnt, self.greeting_cpnt):
            self.components_model.add_component(component)

    def execute(self):
        """Build the greeting from the pulled name."""
        who = self.who_cpnt.pull_value()
        # Not evaluated: a text result would be run as an expression otherwise.
        self.greeting_cpnt.push_value(f"Hello, {who}.", evaluate=False)

Register it in the plugin: plugin.contents.nodes = [GreeterNode]. It shows up in the palette under the plugin's palette name.

docs.title: What a node class defines
docs.text: Member Required Purpose get_type_id() yes Unique id stored in stage files, namespace:name. get_type_display_name() yes Name in the UI. get_description() no One sentence shown in the palette. get_tags() no Set of strings for searching and filtering in the palette. get_type_icon() no Qt resource path of the icon. DEFAULT_NAME no Address name new nodes start with. setup() usually Creates the components. get_type_flags() no NodeFlag values, see below. get_type_execution_order() no BEFORE_CHILDREN (default) or AFTER_CHILDREN. get_render_options() no NodeRenderOptions for how the editor draws the node.

docs.title: Components in setup
docs.text:
• components_model.create_component(type_id) creates a component of a registered type (CoreNodeComponents.VALUE, FLOW, SCRIPT, FILE, COMMENT, or your own). It is not part of the node until add_component adds it. add_component makes the name unique among the node's components.
  • The components setup creates are marked built-in: users can't delete them.
  • Keep a reference on self (self.who_cpnt) to use in evaluate and execute. node["who"] also finds a component by name.
  • The stdlib sets the properties before add_component; do the same.
Property Meaning readable The component is an output: it can be the source of links. writable The component is an input: it accepts a link. is_editable The value can be edited in the UI. is_literal Text is kept as typed instead of being evaluated as an expression. Use for names and paths. is_static Skipped when the node's components execute. set_datatype(type_id) Datatype of the value, see New datatype. default_value, push_value(v) The value to reset to, and the current one. description Tooltip text. component_flags NodeComponentFlag bitmask with all of the above and INHERITS_DATATYPE, INSPECTOR_HIDDEN, SINGLE_OUTPUT.

A flow component is what makes a node part of the execution chain: readable means the flow can continue through it, writable means the flow can arrive through it.

docs.title: When your code runs
docs.text:
For each execution of the node, in this order (see the user guide, How a graph executes):

  1. pre_execution_hook()
  2. evaluate_components(), which evaluates every component value,
  3. evaluate(): decide things from the evaluated inputs. Branch sets which flow output is active here.
  4. execute_components(), which runs components like Script,
  5. execute(): the node's work.
  6. post_execution_hook()

Raise any exception to fail the node: it is logged, the node is marked as failed and the run stops. Write results with push_value(value, evaluate=False) so strings aren't run as Python expressions.

Read inputs with pull_value(). It follows an input link (and casts to the component's datatype) or returns the component's own value. It never runs the node on the other end of the link, so producers must come earlier in the flow.

docs.title: Reacting to edits
docs.text:
on_component_edited(component) is called when a component's value is edited or linked in the editor. Branch uses it to refresh its active outputs, so the editor shows the right path before a run:

def evaluate(self):
    chosen = bool(self.value_cpnt.pull_value())
    self.flow_out_true.is_active = chosen
    self.flow_out_false.is_active = not chosen

def on_component_edited(self, component):
    if component is self.value_cpnt:
        self.evaluate()

docs.title: Containers and scopes
docs.text:
Nodes can contain other nodes. The children of a node run from the node's Flow Start child, while the node's scope is open. A node that wants to give something to its children overrides enter_scope:

from nyx.api.v1 import NodeExecutionContext

def enter_scope(self, context: NodeExecutionContext):
    connection = open_connection()
    context.provide(connection)                    # children find it by type
    context.add_cleanup(connection.close)          # runs when the scope ends, even on failure

Children use self.stage.crawler.context.find(Connection) (or .require(...), which raises LookupError when nothing is provided). Remote Client and Launch Process work like this.

A node that runs the chain behind one of its flow outputs more than once (a loop) calls self.stage.crawler.run_flow_branch(flow_component). Use crawler.wait_for(func, ...) for anything that blocks, so the UI stays alive and the run can be cancelled.

docs.title: Node flags
docs.text:
Return flags from get_type_flags(), adding to the parent's (super() first):

Flag Effect NodeFlag.LOCKS_CHILDREN Nodes inside can't be changed or linked to from outside. Used by Reference. NodeFlag.LOCKS_STRUCTURE Components can't be added, removed, renamed or given another datatype.

docs.title: Saving and loading
docs.text:
A node is saved with its name, position, active state, execution order, components, child nodes, util objects and links. On load Nyx creates the node from its type id, which runs setup, and then restores the saved components over the ones setup made. Consequences:

  • setup must be deterministic and create the same built-in components every time.
  • State you want to keep must live in components (the value of a component is saved), not in Python attributes. Attributes are lost on load. Reset anything per-run in pre_execution_hook.
  • If the type id of a node isn't registered when a stage is opened (the plugin isn't loaded), the registry logs an error naming the id. Keep ids stable.
  • For nodes that get their content from elsewhere (like Reference) override serialize_contents and deserialize_contents.

docs.title: Subclassing an existing node
docs.text: A node class can extend another. Remote Action is meant for it: a subclass adds components and overrides build_script, build_args and handle_response, and leaves execute alone, so a DCC plugin can offer a node with its own script and arguments without any bridge code.

docs.title: New util object
docs.text:
A util object is something that sits in the graph of a node but isn't part of the execution: notes and groups are util objects. It has a position and a size, and properties of its own. It has no components and no links.

A util object needs two classes:

  1. the util object (UtilObject subclass): the data, which is saved with the stage,
  2. a graphics object (a QGraphicsItem) that draws it, see New graphics object.

docs.title: A complete example: a checklist
docs.text:
# studio_tools/util_objects/checklist.py
import typing
from collections import OrderedDict

from nyx.api.v1 import UtilObject, CoreGraphicsObjects


class ChecklistObject(UtilObject):
    """A list of to-do items drawn next to the nodes."""

    DEFAULT_SIZE = (240.0, 160.0)

    ITEMS_KEY = "items"

    def __init__(self, uuid=None):
        """Initialize ChecklistObject.

        Args:
            uuid (UUID | str | None): object uuid. Generated if omitted.
        """
        super().__init__(uuid=uuid)
        self.items: list[str] = []

    @classmethod
    def get_type_id(cls) -> str:
        """str: util object type id."""
        return "studio:checklist"

    @classmethod
    def get_type_display_name(cls) -> str:
        """str: name shown in the UI."""
        return "Checklist"

    @classmethod
    def get_description(cls) -> str:
        """str: what the type does."""
        return "A list of to-do items."

    @classmethod
    def get_graphics_object_id(cls) -> str | None:
        """str | None: id of the graphics object drawing the type."""
        return "studio.checklist"

    def serialize_properties(self) -> OrderedDict[str, typing.Any]:
        """OrderedDict[str, typing.Any]: position, size and the items."""
        properties = super().serialize_properties()
        properties[self.ITEMS_KEY] = list(self.items)
        return properties

    def apply_properties(self, properties: typing.Mapping[str, typing.Any]) -> None:
        """Set position, size and the items.

        Args:
            properties (typing.Mapping[str, typing.Any]): values by name.
        """
        super().apply_properties(properties)
        if self.ITEMS_KEY in properties:
            self.items = [str(item) for item in properties[self.ITEMS_KEY]]

Register: plugin.contents.util_objects = [ChecklistObject].

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
Member Purpose get_type_id() Unique id, namespace:name. get_type_display_name(), get_description() UI texts. get_graphics_object_id() The id of the graphics object that draws the type. It must be registered by a plugin (or be a built-in one such as CoreGraphicsObjects.NOTE). DEFAULT_SIZE, MIN_SIZE Size a new object gets, and the smallest size it can be resized to. position, size, rect Geometry in the scene of the owning node. The size is never smaller than MIN_SIZE. serialize_properties() Returns all state that can change, as JSON values. Call super() and add your own. apply_properties(properties) Sets the state from such a mapping. Missing names are left unchanged. node, stage, path, is_locked The owner and the state: is_locked is true inside a locked scope (the content of a reference).

serialize_properties and apply_properties are the whole contract of state. They are used for saving, loading, copy and paste, and by the undo commands, which store the properties before and after a change and apply them on undo and redo. If a piece of state isn't in them, it is lost on save and can't be undone. Keep attributes (self.items) plain and let the properties mirror them.

docs.title: Creating and changing util objects
docs.text:
The editor offers Create note and Create group in the context menu of the graph. Other util objects aren't offered in the UI by default: a plugin creates them from code, or from its own action, with a command (so undo works):

from nyx.api.v1 import commands

command = commands.CreateUtilObjectCommand(
    stage=stage,
    type_id="studio:checklist",
    node=parent_node,                  # defaults to the stage root
    position=(120.0, 40.0),
    properties={"items": ["Export", "Review"]},
)
stage.push_command(command)
checklist = command.result_object

To change one, push a SetUtilObjectPropertiesCommand with the new properties by object:

stage.push_command(
    commands.SetUtilObjectPropertiesCommand(
        stage, {checklist: {"items": ["Export", "Review", "Publish"]}}, text="Edit checklist"
    )
)

The graphics object does that for you when the user moves or resizes it, see below. DeleteUtilObjectCommand removes one.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Util objects are written to the util_objects list of their node, with their type id and their properties (serialize_properties).

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Util objects never take part in execution. If something has to run, make it a node.
  • They don't have components, so values can't be linked to them. To show data from the graph, use a node.
  • A color, text or title is a property of the object, not a config option. Defaults can come from the config with nyx.core.util_object.get_configured_color as the note does.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: Nyx is a nodal execution graph. You build a stage out of nodes, connect their components with links, and run it, in the editor or from the command line.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Install Nyx and open the editor, see the README.
  2. Read How a graph executes to understand flow links, data links and evaluation. Everything else builds on it.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Page What you learn How a graph executes How the flow moves from node to node, what a node does when it runs, how values are evaluated and pulled. Datatypes The built-in datatypes, which components can be linked, and how values are converted. Link pins Routing a link through dots you place on it. Built-ins A page for every component, node and utility object of the standard library. Referencing stages Reusing a stage file inside another stage.
