Looking to extend Nyx with your own nodes? See the Developer Guide.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text: Term Meaning Stage A graph document, saved as a .nyx file. Node A box in the graph. Can contain other nodes. Component A plug on a node: a value, a flow connection, a script, ... Link A connection between two components. Pin A dot on a link that the link is drawn through, see Link pins. Flow The path of execution, drawn with white pentagon plugs. Scope The inside of a node. The stage root is the outermost scope. Util object A note or a group. Organizes a graph, doesn't execute. Plugin A package providing nodes, components, datatypes and other content. Bridge The link to external processes, see Remote nodes.

docs.title: Running stages in batch mode
docs.text: A stage doesn't need the editor to run. The command line loads the plugins, loads the stage, runs it once and exits with a code that tells you how it went. Use it for scheduled jobs, render farms, build servers and anywhere else no one is there to press a button.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text:
nyx stage run path/to/stage.nyx
nyx-run-stage path/to/stage.nyx         # the same, as one command

Both are installed with the package, and with the standalone app (see the README).

Option Effect --no-bridge Don't start the bridge server. Use it for stages without Remote nodes, or when the port is needed elsewhere. --port N Use port N for the bridge server in this run instead of the configured one. Handy when several runs happen on one machine at once.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The stage ran. 1 The stage failed. The log names the node that failed and the error. 2 The file doesn't exist or couldn't be loaded. 130 Interrupted with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: What a run does
docs.text:
1. Starts a Qt application without a window. QT_QPA_PLATFORM defaults to offscreen, so no display is needed (servers, containers, CI).
  2. Loads the config and the plugins, including those from plugin_paths and NYX_PLUGIN_PATH.
  3. Loads the stage file. References are resolved relative to it.
  4. Starts the bridge server unless --no-bridge is given or the config disables it.
  5. Runs the stage once, from the root, following the flow as described in How a graph executes, and then shuts the session down.

The config is read but never saved. Nothing is written to your user config by a batch run, so runs are safe on a machine you also use for editing.

Note

A run executes the stage as it is on disk. There is no command line parameter for component values. Set the inputs of a batch from outside with the things a graph can read: environment variables (the Get Env function node), files, or a small wrapper stage that references the real one and sets its components.

docs.title: Running many stages
docs.text:
Each run is a process, so the shell does the batching.

# one after another, stop at the first failure
for stage in stages/*.nyx; do
    nyx-run-stage --no-bridge "$stage" || exit 1
done

# all of them, then count the failures
failed=0
for stage in stages/*.nyx; do
    nyx-run-stage --no-bridge "$stage" || failed=$((failed + 1))
done
echo "$failed failed"

# in parallel, four at a time
ls stages/*.nyx | xargs -P 4 -n 1 nyx-run-stage --no-bridge

Stages that need DCC clients and run in parallel must not share a bridge port: give each run its own --port, and a Remote Client node that waits for the client it started with Launch Process.

From Python:

import pathlib
import subprocess

results = {}
for stage in sorted(pathlib.Path("stages").glob("*.nyx")):
    completed = subprocess.run(["nyx-run-stage", "--no-bridge", str(stage)])
    results[stage.name] = completed.returncode

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: The messages go to the console and to the log file in the logs folder of the user directory. Every executed node logs its path and how long it took, and a failure logs the node and the exception with its traceback. logging_level in the config (or NYX_DEBUG=1) makes it more verbose.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text:
The standalone app and the package both work. With the package and uv:

- uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
- run: uv sync --locked
- run: uv run nyx-run-stage --no-bridge stages/nightly.nyx

A non-zero exit code fails the job.

docs.title: From your own code
docs.text:
To drive stages from Python without a subprocess, create the application and a stage and start its crawler, like the CLI does:

from nyx.api.v1 import Stage
from nyx.application import NyxApplication

app = NyxApplication()          # needs QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen without a display
stage = Stage()                 # keep the reference, nodes don't hold the stage
if stage.import_json("stages/nightly.nyx") is None:
    raise SystemExit("could not load the stage")

failed = []
stage.execution_failed.connect(failed.append)
try:
    stage.crawler.start()
except Exception:
    print("failed at", failed[0].path if failed else "the stage")

stage.crawler.request_cancel() asks a running crawl to stop. Connect to the stage signals (execution_started, execution_succeeded, execution_finished, execution_failed, execution_cancelled) to follow a run.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text: Nyx keeps its settings in one JSON file, the user config. The editor reads it at startup, and saves it when it exits normally, with state such as the window layout and the recent files. Edit it by hand to change options, or to prepare a machine. Close the editor first, or it overwrites your edit when it exits.

docs.title: Where the files are
docs.text:
All user files live in one directory:

Platform Directory Linux, macOS $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nyx, ~/.config/nyx when the variable is not set Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\sowwic\nyx File Content user_config.json The config described on this page session.nyxsession Stages that were open when the editor closed bridge.json Address and token of the running bridge server, see Remote nodes logs/ Log files profiling/ .pstats files, see the developer guide

make config-file prints the path of the config file. A missing file or key falls back to the default, so the file only has to hold what you change. A stage run with nyx stage run reads the config but never saves it.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Effect NYX_PLUGIN_PATH Extra directories to search for plugins, in addition to the plugin_paths config value. Separated by : on Linux and macOS, ; on Windows. NYX_DEBUG 1 logs at debug level and shows the model roles as a tooltip on nodes and plugs. NYX_PROFILING 1 writes profiler files for the profiled steps, see the developer guide. XDG_CONFIG_HOME Moves the user directory (Linux, macOS).

docs.title: Config reference
docs.text:
The file is a tree of sections. Defaults are shown; paths such as editor_widgets.graphics_stage.link_style mean nested objects.

{
    "bridge": { "enabled": true, "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": null, "token": "" },
    "editor_style": { "dark_mode": true },
    "plugin_paths": ["~/nyx_plugins"]
}

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Option Default Description logging_level 20 Logging level of the application, the numbers of Python's logging (10 debug, 20 info, 30 warning, 40 error). plugin_paths [] Extra directories to search for nyx_plugin.py files. ~ is expanded. Directories that do not exist are reported in the log and skipped.

docs.title: bridge
docs.text:
The server external processes (Maya, Blender, ...) connect to. See Remote nodes.

Option Default Description enabled true Start the server when the application launches. It can be started later from the Bridge dock. host "127.0.0.1" Interface to listen on. Anyone holding the token can run code in a client, so only change it on a network you trust. port null Port to listen on. null tries the default port and the ones after it. token "" Secret clients have to present. Random on every launch if empty. Set it to keep a fixed token across launches.

docs.title: editor_behaviour
docs.text: Option Default Description new_stage_on_launch true Create an empty stage at startup. show_splash_screen true Show a splash screen with the startup progress. show_address_names false Show the address names of nodes and components (the names paths are made of) instead of their display names. undo_limit 100 Undoable steps each stage remembers, 0 for no limit. Applies to stages opened after the change. Deleting and pasting nodes keep a copy of them, so a high limit costs memory on big stages.

docs.title: editor_session
docs.text:
State the editor maintains itself.

Option Default Description recent_files [] Recently used stage files, most recent first. Files that no longer exist are dropped when the config is loaded and saved. max_recent_files 10 Number of recent files that are kept.

docs.title: main_window
docs.text:
Saved when the window closes.

Option Default Description size null Window size in pixels, [width, height]. position null Window position on the screen, [x, y]. is_always_on_top false Keep the window above other windows. layout.version 0 Layout version the state was saved with. layout.state null Base64 encoded Qt window state (the arrangement of the docks). Set it to null to reset the layout.

docs.title: editor_style
docs.text: Option Default Description dark_mode true Use the dark palette. animations.link_pulse.color "#4BE3FF" Color of the dot and its tail, a color name or #RRGGBB. animations.link_pulse.speed 160.0 Scene units the dot travels per second. animations.link_pulse.radius 5 Radius of the dot in scene units. animations.link_pulse.tail_samples 6 Number of dots the tail is made of. animations.link_pulse.tail_step 6.0 Scene units between the dots of the tail. animations.link_glow.color "#4BE3FF" Color of the halo. animations.link_glow.period 1.6 Seconds for the glow to swell and fade once. animations.link_glow.layers [[12.0, 0.15], [8.0, 0.25], [4.0, 0.4]] Strokes the halo is made of, as [width, opacity] pairs. The width is in scene units, the opacity is the one at full intensity.

docs.title: editor_widgets
docs.text: Option Default Description log_widget.auto_scroll true Scroll the log to new records. log_widget.is_expanded false The log dock is expanded. log_widget.expanded_height 220 Height of the expanded log dock in pixels. log_widget.minimum_level 10 Minimum logging level shown in the log. graphics_stage.link_style "bezier" Shape links are drawn with: bezier, direct or square. graphics_stage.highlight_flow_chain true Animate the flow links that are part of the execution chain of the drawn scope. graphics_stage.highlight_flow_chain_style "pulse" Animation that highlights the chain: pulse or glow. graphics_stage.background_style "grid" Pattern of the stage background: grid or dots. graphics_stage.background_color "#393939" Fill color of the stage background. graphics_stage.default_note_color "#e8c95a" Color new notes get. graphics_stage.default_group_color "#5b8def" Color new groups get. graphics_stage.viewport_debug_overlay false Show performance numbers over the graph views. graphics_stage.nodes.hover_diagnostics false Show the model roles as a tooltip when hovering nodes and plugs.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: NyxConfig is a layered config from the json-config package. The user file is its root layer, and Nyx registers no other. Plugin authors reach the resolved config of the running application with nyx.core.layered_config.get_app_config(), whose values attribute has the sections above as typed objects (config.values.bridge.port).

docs.title: Datatypes
docs.text:
A datatype describes the kind of value a component holds. It decides three things:

  • how the plug looks (color and shape), so you can read a graph at a glance,
  • which components can be linked together,
  • how a value is converted when it arrives in or is stored on a component.

Datatypes are provided by plugins and identified by a type id with a namespace, such as core:int. The ones below are always available.

docs.title: Built-in datatypes
docs.text:
Type id Name Python type Default Plug core:object Object any None blue square matrix core:type Type type object purple circle core:bool Boolean bool False red circle core:string String str "" orange circle core:int Integer int 0 green-teal circle core:float Float float 0.0 light green circle core:path Path pathlib.PurePosixPath none light blue circle core:list List list [] pink bars core:dict Dictionary dict {} yellow diamond core:flow Flow none none white pentagon core:stage_object_path Object Path none none blue square

Flow and Object Path belong to specific component types and can't be picked as the datatype of a value component. All others can, using the datatype selector of a value component or the set_datatype method.

Object is the datatype of values without a hint: whenever a component has no datatype set (or a plugin that provided it isn't loaded) it is treated as Object.

docs.title: Which components can be linked
docs.text:
When you drag a link, the target component asks whether it accepts the datatype of the source. The rules, in order:

  1. The same datatype is always accepted.
  2. A datatype can name others it is compatible with. Integer and Float accept each other, Object Path accepts String.
  3. Flow ignores wildcards. A flow component only links to another flow component, and a data component can never be linked to flow.
  4. Otherwise the link is accepted when either side is a wildcard. Object, Type, Boolean and String are wildcards: they link to everything but flow.
from \ to Object Bool String Int Float Path List Dict Flow Object yes yes yes yes yes yes yes yes no Bool, String, Type yes yes yes yes yes yes yes yes no Int yes yes yes yes yes no no no no Float yes yes yes yes yes no no no no Path, List, Dict yes yes yes no no same only same only same only no Flow no no no no no no no no yes

Linking is the permission; what actually arrives is decided by casting.

docs.title: Casting
docs.text:
Every datatype has a caster, a function that converts a value to the datatype. It is applied:

  • when a text value is evaluated on a component. The text is first evaluated as a Python expression (see How a graph executes), then the result is cast: 3.7 typed into an Integer component becomes 3.
  • when a value is pulled through a link. The value of the source is cast to the datatype of the target. A value that can't be cast is logged as a warning (naming the component and the reason) and passed on unchanged.
  • when a Setter node pushes a value into a component, or a Type Cast node converts a value.

A value that can't be cast to the datatype of its own component makes the component invalid: the reason is shown on it.

The casters are the obvious ones: bool, str, int, float, list, dict, PurePosixPath for paths. Type also accepts the id of a registered datatype, and a datatype or any value, from which it takes the Python type.

docs.title: Wildcards are not "any value"
docs.text: A wildcard only means the link is allowed. Linking a String component to an Integer component works, and at run time "12" is cast to 12, but "abc" fails with a warning and keeps arriving as text. Use a Type Cast node when you want the conversion to be explicit, and Get Type to inspect the type of a value.

docs.title: Datatypes of function nodes
docs.text: Function nodes (see the developer guide) pick the datatype of each parameter from its type hint. X | None counts as X, and a generic such as list[str] as the class it is made from, list. The first registered datatype whose Python type is exactly that class is used: int becomes Integer, list becomes List, and so on. A parameter without a hint, or with a hint no datatype claims (pathlib.Path, a union of several types), is an Object. Datatypes added by plugins take part in this lookup too.

docs.title: Inherited datatypes
docs.text: Some components don't have a datatype of their own. They follow the component they take their value from. The value of a Setter node is an example: it takes the datatype of what is linked to it, and you can choose one while nothing is linked.

docs.title: How a graph executes
docs.text: This page explains what happens when you run a stage: in which order nodes run, what a node does when it runs, and how values travel between components.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text:
Piece What it is Stage The document. It holds one root node, /stage, and the undo history. A stage file has the extension .nyx. Node A box in the graph. It has components, and may contain other nodes (its children). Every node is addressed by a path such as /stage/loop/log. Component A plug on a node: a value, a flow connection, a script, a file path, a comment. A component is writable (accepts a link into it), readable (can be the source of links), or both. Link A connection from a readable component to a writable one. Scope The inside of a node. The root node is the scope of the whole stage; a node containing children is the scope of those children.

There are two kinds of links, and they do different jobs:

  • Flow links join flow components (white pentagon plugs). They say which node runs next. They carry no data.
  • Data links join all other components. They say where a value comes from.

docs.title: Execution flow: from node to node
docs.text:
Execution does not run every node in the stage. It follows the flow links.

  1. Each scope has a Flow Start node. The crawler looks for the Flow Start child of a scope and begins there. A scope without a Flow Start node runs none of its children.
  2. Flow follows the flow components. After a node has run, the crawler looks at the node's flow components that are readable (outputs) and active, and runs the node each of them is linked to. Those nodes are siblings: a flow link can only join nodes in the same scope, anything else is an error.
  3. A node's children run with the node. When the crawler reaches a node that contains other nodes, it also runs the inside of it, from the Flow Start node of that scope. By default the node itself runs first and then its children (BEFORE_CHILDREN); a node can be set to run after its children (AFTER_CHILDREN).
  4. The scope is finished before the flow moves on. The next sibling runs only after the node and everything inside it are done. The order is depth first.
/stage
 ├─ Flow Start ──▶ Branch ──true──▶ Log "yes" ──▶ Container
 │                    └────false─▶ Log "no"         ├─ Flow Start ──▶ Log "inside"
 │                                                    └ ...

If Branch picks true, the order is: Flow Start, Branch, Log "yes", Container, Flow Start (inside), Log "inside". Log "no" never runs.

docs.title: Active and inactive
docs.text:
Two switches decide whether something takes part:

  • A node can be deactivated. An inactive node is skipped, and so the flow stops there.
  • A flow component can be inactive. Before a node is evaluated all its flow outputs are active. Nodes that make a decision switch some off while they evaluate:
Node Behavior Branch Activates true or false depending on its condition. Sequence Several outputs are active at once. Each is followed completely, depth first, one after another. For Loop, For Each Loop, While Loop Run the chain behind their loop_body output again and again, then continue with completed.

A decision is made after the node is evaluated, never guessed ahead of time. This is also what the editor shows when it animates the links of the execution chain.

docs.title: Visited once
docs.text: A node runs at most once per run. If two paths converge on a node, or the links form a cycle, the node is not run again and a warning goes to the log. Loop nodes are the way to repeat: they run their body chain several times and reset what was visited inside it each time.

docs.title: Scopes can provide things to their children
docs.text: Because the inside of a node runs while the node's scope is open, a node can hand something to the nodes inside it, and have it cleaned up when they are done, however they end. This is how Remote Client gives its connection to the Remote Action nodes inside it, see Remote nodes.

docs.title: What happens when a node runs
docs.text:
For one node the crawler calls execution_hook, which does this:

  1. Reset the status of the node. Stop here if the node is inactive.
  2. Set the status to pending and call pre_execution_hook.
  3. Evaluate the components. For every component in order: clear its cached value, skip it if it is inactive, otherwise evaluate its value (see below), then call the component's own evaluate.
  4. Call the node's evaluate. Nodes that decide something (like Branch) do it here.
  5. Execute the components. For every component in order: skip it if it is static or inactive, otherwise call the component's execute (a Script component runs its file here).
  6. Call the node's execute. This is the node's work: log a message, call the function, send code to a remote client.
  7. Call post_execution_hook.

If anything raises, the error is logged, the node gets the error status, the stage emits execution_failed with the node and the exception stops the whole run. The editor marks the node and the CLI exits with code 1. A run can also be cancelled; it ends quietly and the scopes are cleaned up.

The stage reports the run through signals: execution_started, then execution_succeeded and execution_finished, or execution_failed, or execution_cancelled.

docs.title: Evaluation and values
docs.text:
Every value component holds three things: the raw value (what you typed or what was pushed), the cached value (the evaluated result) and the display text.

Evaluating a component turns the raw value into the cached value:

  • A text value is evaluated as a Python expression: 1 + 2 gives 3, [1, 2, 3] gives a list. If it can't be evaluated, the text stays as it is. Components flagged literal (script paths, file paths, client names, ...) keep text as typed. Expressions run with Python's eval, so a stage can run arbitrary code: open and run only stages you trust, like you would a script.
  • The result is cast to the datatype of the component, see Datatypes. A value that can't be cast makes the component invalid; the reason is shown on it.

Pulling a value is what a node does when it needs an input, with component.pull_value():

  • If the component has an input link, the value comes from the source component of the link (pull_value of that component, recursively), cast to the datatype of this component. A failed cast is logged as a warning and the value is passed on as it is.
  • Otherwise the component's own cached value is used.

Important

Pulling does not run the source node. It reads the value the source component holds now. A value link only gives you the right value if the node that produces it has already run, so order nodes with flow links: the producer before the consumer.

This is why a graph is built from two things working together: flow links for when, data links for what.

docs.title: Reading and writing other components
docs.text: A Setter node pushes a value into any component, found by its path (/stage/counter.value), cast to that component's datatype. A Getter node reads one. They let a graph keep state across nodes without a link between them. Both run in flow order like any other node.

docs.title: Functions and scripts
docs.text:
• A function node has one value component per parameter and one for the return value (return). When it runs it pulls the parameters, calls the function and stores the result in return.
  • A Script component runs a Python file, or a module:function entry point, when its node executes. The script sees nyx_node and nyx_cpnt as globals.

docs.title: Other things worth knowing
docs.text:
• The UI stays alive during a run. The crawler lets the application process events regularly. Long waits (a remote client, a process) happen in a helper thread so the run can still be cancelled.
  • Util objects (notes and groups) are not part of the execution. They help you organize a graph.
  • To run a graph without the editor, see Running stages in batch mode.

docs.title: Link pins
docs.text:
A link is drawn from the output plug of one component to the input plug of another. When a graph grows, links run across nodes or bend in ways that are hard to follow. A pin is a small dot you put on a link: the link is drawn through it, so you decide where it goes.

Pins only change how a link is drawn. They have no effect on execution, on the values the link carries, or on which components are connected.

docs.title: Using pins
docs.text:
To Do Add a pin Double-click the link. The pin appears under the cursor. Move a pin Drag it. The link follows while you drag. Remove a pin Double-click the pin.

A link can have as many pins as you need. A new pin goes into the part of the link that passes closest to where you clicked, so the link goes through the pins in the order they are along it, from the source to the target.

Things to know:

  • A pin belongs to one link. Links don't share pins, and deleting a link deletes its pins.
  • Pins are free: they don't snap to the grid and aren't attached to a node. Moving a node doesn't move the pins of its links.
  • A pin has the color of the plug the link comes from. For a link between plugs of different colors, that is the color of the source end.
  • Every change is a step in the undo history, adding, moving and removing a pin each. Undoing the removal of a link, or of the node it connects, brings its pins back.
  • Pins can't be changed on links of a referenced stage, like any other part of it.

docs.title: Pins and the link style
docs.text: The pins stay the same whichever style the links are drawn in. Each part of the link, from the source to the first pin, between pins, and from the last pin to the target, is drawn in the configured graphics_stage.link_style (bezier, direct or square), see Customization.

docs.title: Saved with the stage
docs.text: Pins are saved in the .nyx file, inside the link they belong to. Stages saved before pins existed open as before, and a link without pins doesn't write anything extra.

docs.title: Referencing stages
docs.text: A Reference node (core:reference) stands for another stage file. Use it to build a graph out of smaller, reusable stages: a "publish a file" stage that you drop into many pipelines, a shared setup, a sub-graph one person maintains for the team.

docs.title: What a reference is
docs.text:
The top node of the stage file you point to (its root, /stage) has components: the inputs and outputs the author of that stage chose to expose. The Reference node gets the same components. The nodes inside the source file become its children.

build_scene.nyx                         main.nyx
/stage                                  /stage
 ├ components: scene_path, result        ├ Flow Start ─▶ reference ─▶ Log
 ├ Flow Start ─▶ Open ─▶ Export          │               source = build_scene.nyx
 └ ...                                   │               scene_path = "a.ma"
                                         │               result  ───────────────┘
                                         └ (Open, Export, ... as locked children)

When the stage runs, the Reference node behaves like any node that contains children: it runs, then the crawler runs the inside from its Flow Start node, then the flow continues to the next sibling.

docs.title: Using a reference
docs.text:
1. Create a Reference node.
  2. Set its source: a path to a .nyx file. A relative path is relative to the folder of the stage file the reference is in, or, for a reference inside another reference, to the folder of that source file. An unsaved stage can only use absolute paths.
  3. The components of the source stage appear on the node. Give them values or link them like components of any node.

The node's subtitle shows the file name, or the reason the source could not be loaded (missing file, not a .nyx file, unreadable, no source set).

docs.title: What you can and can't change
docs.text:
A reference is a view of its source, so the source stays in charge of its shape:

You can You can't Set the values of its components Add, remove or rename components Link to and from its components Change the datatype of a component Deactivate the node Edit, add or delete the nodes inside Look inside the node Link to or from nodes inside from the outside

To change what is inside, open and edit the source stage itself.

docs.title: Saving and reloading
docs.text:
• The stage file stores the reference node's own settings: the source path, the values you set on its components, and links to the outside. It does not store the nodes inside. They are loaded from the source again every time the stage is opened, so edits to the source show up in every stage that references it.
  • Use Reload reference from the node's context menu after editing its source while the stage is open. Reloading keeps the values you set and the links to its components. The context menu of a reference node can also open the source stage in the editor.
  • A reload clears the undo history of the stage, because it is not a change the history could undo.
  • If the author of the source renames a component, the reference recognizes it (it matches components by their identity first, then by name) and keeps your value and links. A component that was removed from the source, or whose type changed, stays on the node marked as invalid with the reason, so you can see which links to remove. If the source can't be loaded, all components stay with the error as the reason and nothing is lost.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A stage cannot reference itself, directly or through another reference.
  • The source must be a .nyx file that exists.
  • A source cannot have a component named source, since the reference node uses that name for its own source setting. It is left out, with a warning in the log.
  • References can be nested: the source may contain references of its own.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Treat the components of a stage you plan to reference as its API. Give them clear names and descriptions, and mark outputs as readable and inputs as writable.
  • Keep referenced stages in the same repository as the stages that use them and use relative sources, so the whole set can be moved or checked out elsewhere.
  • Run a referenced stage in batch mode on its own to test it.

docs.title: Remote nodes and the bridge
docs.text: Some work can only be done inside another application: build a scene in Maya, export a mesh from Blender, call an API that only exists in a DCC's Python. Nyx doesn't import those applications. It sends code to them over the bridge and takes the results back into the graph.

docs.title: The concept
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────┐         TCP          ┌───────────────────────────┐
│ Nyx (server)             │ ◀──────────────────  │ Maya / Blender / any      │
│  BridgeServer            │   client connects    │ Python (client)           │
│  Remote Client node      │ ──── code ─────────▶ │  NyxClient                │
│   └ Remote Action nodes  │ ◀─── result ──────── │  runs it on the app's     │
└──────────────────────────┘                      │  main thread              │
                                                  └───────────────────────────┘
  • Nyx is the server; the external process is the client and connects out. The process that executes code never opens a port.
  • One server per application. Many clients can be connected at once, each with a name and a kind (maya, blender, python, ...).
  • Clients find the server through an address file, bridge.json in the Nyx user directory, which holds the host, port and a token. On the same machine nothing needs to be configured. A client can also be given the address and token directly, or through the environment variables NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN and NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS_FILE.
  • A token protects the server. Whoever has the token can run code in a connected client, so the server listens on 127.0.0.1 by default and generates a random token at every launch (unless you set bridge.token). The address file is readable by its owner only where the system supports it.

The protocol, the server and the client base class live in a separate package, nyx-bridge. It has no dependencies and does not import Nyx or Qt, so it installs into the Python of a DCC. The DCC specific parts are separate repositories:

Repository What it adds nyx-bridge-maya A Maya client (plug-in and Python API) and a Nyx plugin with Maya nodes. nyx-bridge-blender A Blender add-on client and a Nyx plugin with Blender nodes.

Install the client half into the DCC following the README of the repository, and the Nyx half by adding the plugin folder to plugin_paths or NYX_PLUGIN_PATH (see Customization).

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text: The server starts with the application when bridge.enabled is true (the default). The Bridge dock of the editor shows its address, the connected clients, and lets you start, stop and copy the address or token. With nyx stage run the server starts too, unless --no-bridge is given, so a headless run can reach clients as well. bridge.port fixes the port (--port N overrides it for one headless run); when it is null the default port is tried first and then the ones after it.

docs.title: Remote Client
docs.text:
A scope node. It waits until a matching client has connected, then runs the nodes inside it with that client available to them.

Component Purpose client_name Name of the client to wait for. Empty accepts any. client_kind Kind of the client (maya, blender, ...). Empty accepts any. timeout Seconds to wait for a client before failing, 30 by default. 0 or less waits forever. client (output) Name of the connected client.

If more than one connected client matches, the node fails instead of picking one, so code never goes to the wrong application. Set the name or kind to choose. If no client connects in time it fails with a message naming the address it waited on.

The wait doesn't freeze the editor and can be cancelled.

docs.title: Remote Action
docs.text:
A flow node that must be placed inside a Remote Client (its scope), because it asks that scope for the client. It sends a script to the client and waits for the answer.

Component Purpose script A Python file, or an entry point module:function. args A dictionary of values the script can use by name. timeout Seconds to wait for the answer, 30 by default. 0 or less waits forever. response (output) The value the script assigned to result.

How the script is run depends on what script holds:

  • A file. The file is read in Nyx and its source is sent. The entries of args are variables in the script. To send something back, assign it to result:

    # export_selection.py, runs inside Maya
# `args` entries are variables: `path`
cmds.file(path, exportSelected=True, type="mayaAscii")
result = cmds.ls(selection=True)

  • An entry point, package.module:function. The module must be importable in the client. It is imported there and called with the entries of args as keyword arguments, and its return value becomes the result. The part before the colon can go through attributes, like bpy.ops.mesh:primitive_cube_add.

Everything crossing the bridge has to be JSON data: numbers, strings, booleans, lists, dictionaries and None. Anything else arrives as its repr. Standard output and standard error of the script are written to the Nyx log. An exception in the client is raised in the Remote Action node as a RemoteExecutionError with the traceback of the client, so the node fails like any other. The code runs on the main thread of the application, as the DCC requires.

Plugins can subclass Remote Action to build the script and its arguments themselves, so that a node for a DCC doesn't need you to write one, see the developer guide.

docs.title: Launch Process
docs.text:
Optional. A scope node that starts the external process instead of waiting for you to start it, for example a headless Blender, and stops it when the nodes inside are done.

Component Purpose command Command line to run. $NAME and ${NAME} are replaced by environment variables, those of env included. env Dictionary of environment variables added to the application's. working_directory Folder to run in. Empty uses the current one. client_name Name the process connects as. Empty makes one up. wait_for_client Wait until the process has connected before the nodes inside run. timeout Seconds to wait for it to connect, 30 by default. client, process_id (outputs) Name the process connects as, and its process id.

The process gets NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN and a client name in its environment, so a client started in it connects to this server without any setup. Its output is written to the log line by line, and the last lines are kept for the error message if it fails.

A Remote Client placed inside a Launch Process waits for the process that was started, unless you give it a name or kind of its own.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
Flow Start ─▶ Launch Process ("blender --background --python start_client.py")
               └─ Remote Client (kind = blender)
                   └─ Flow Start ─▶ Remote Action (bpy.ops.mesh:primitive_cube_add)
                                       ─▶ Remote Action (export.py, args = {"path": "cube.fbx"})
               ─▶ Log (response of the export)

When this stage runs: Blender starts and connects, the Remote Client finds it, the actions run in it one after another, then Blender is stopped and the flow goes on to the Log node.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause The bridge server is not running The server is disabled (bridge.enabled), failed to start (see the log), or the stage was run with --no-bridge. No matching client connected to host:port within Ns The client didn't start, got the wrong address or token, or its name or kind doesn't match. Check the Bridge dock for connected clients. N connected clients match, set the client name or kind Several clients are connected. Fill client_name or client_kind. The Remote Action fails with a client traceback The code raised in the external process. Fix the script, the stack trace is the client's. The action doesn't find a client It isn't inside a Remote Client.

docs.title: Built-ins
docs.text:
The stdlib is the plugin every other plugin builds on. It provides the components, nodes and utility objects listed here, shown in the Core section of the nodes palette. For the rules they follow, see How a graph executes; for the datatypes of their values, see Datatypes.

Section Contents Nodes Flow control, loops, values and data, logging, the bridge. Components The plugs nodes are made of. Utility objects Notes and groups.

Other plugins add nodes of their own, for example the path nodes made from plain Python functions. They appear in their own sections of the palette.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
A component is a plug on a node. Nodes are made of them, and you can add them to a node yourself.

Name What it does Comment Static text for notes. Does not take part in execution. Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. Value Holds a typed value that can be edited, linked to other components or pulled by them. Script Runs a python file or a module entry point when the node executes. Remote Script Names a python file or a module entry point to run in an external process, instead of in the application. File Holds the path of a file, typed or picked with a file dialog. Object Path Holds the path of a node or component in the stage and resolves it to the object.

docs.title: Comment
docs.text:
Static text for notes. Does not take part in execution.

Type id: core:comment

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Static, editable text, starts expanded. Its datatype is string.
  • It takes no part in execution.

docs.title: File
docs.text:
Holds the path of a file, typed or picked with a file dialog.

Type id: core:file

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Static and editable. The path is kept as a string.
  • Type the path or pick it with a file dialog.

docs.title: Used by
docs.text: • Reference

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
Connects the execution flow from one node to the next.

Type id: core:flow

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• White pentagon plug. It links only to other flow components, and a data component can never be linked to it.
  • Carries no data: it says which node runs next. Links of the flow are drawn twice as thick as the others.
  • A flow component has a single output link. A node can be active or inactive; nodes that make a decision, like Branch, switch some of their flow outputs off.
  • See How a graph executes.

docs.title: Used by
docs.text:
• Set
  • Action
  • Branch
  • For Loop
  • For Each Loop
  • While Loop
  • Flow Start
  • Sequence
  • Log
  • Type Cast
  • Get Type
  • Remote Client
  • Remote Action
  • Launch Process

docs.title: Remote Script
docs.text:
Names a python file or a module entry point to run in an external process, instead of in the application.

Type id: core:remote_script

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Like Script, but it does nothing in the application: the script runs in the external process of the Remote Client the node is inside of.
  • See Remote nodes and the bridge.

docs.title: Used by
docs.text: • Remote Action

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Runs a python file or a module entry point when the node executes.

Type id: core:script

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Runs when the node executes.
  • The value is either the path of a Python file, or a module:function entry point. It is literal: the path is never evaluated as an expression.
  • Editable, starts expanded.

docs.title: Object Path
docs.text:
Holds the path of a node or component in the stage and resolves it to the object.

Type id: core:stage_object_path

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Holds a path like /stage/node.component. Absolute paths and paths relative to the scope of the owner both work.
  • Resolves the path to the node or component it points at. It is empty until the path points at something that exists.
  • Has a datatype of its own, which also accepts a string.

docs.title: Used by
docs.text:
• Set
  • Get

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
Holds a typed value that can be edited, linked to other components or pulled by them.

Type id: core:value

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Static and editable: you can type the value, link another component into it, or have other components pull it.
  • Pick its datatype with the datatype selector, see Datatypes. Without one it is shown with the datatype of the value it holds.
  • Most inputs and outputs of the built-in nodes are value components.

docs.text:
• Set
  • Get
  • Value
  • Branch
  • Dict
  • List
  • For Loop
  • For Each Loop
  • While Loop
  • Log
  • Type Cast
  • Get Type
  • Remote Client

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text: The nodes of the standard library. Most have flow components that connect them to the execution flow. Nodes without any provide values and run when something pulls from them.

docs.title: Structure and flow control
docs.text: Name What it does Node Empty node without components. Groups other nodes inside of it. Flow Start Marks where the execution flow of the parent scope begins. Action Runs its components when the flow reaches it. A general purpose step with a flow input and output. Branch Continues through the true or false flow output depending on the condition value. Sequence Continues through all of its flow outputs one after another, in order. Reference Stands for a stage file, with the components of its top node.

docs.title: Loops
docs.text: Name What it does For Loop Runs the loop body for every index from the first to the last index, then continues with completed. For Each Loop Runs the loop body for every element of an iterable, optionally in reverse, then continues with completed. While Loop Runs the loop body for as long as the condition is true, then continues with completed.

docs.title: Values and data
docs.text: Name What it does Value Provides a value that can be edited and linked to other nodes. Set Sets the value of a component of another node when the flow reaches it. Get Provides the value of a component of another node. Dict Collects value components and creates a dictionary result. List Collects value components and creates a list result. Type Cast Converts an object to the given type when the flow reaches it, e.g. a string to an int. Get Type Finds the type of an object when the flow reaches it.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Name What it does Log Writes a message to the log with the chosen level.

docs.title: Bridge and processes
docs.text: Name What it does Remote Client Waits for an external process to connect to the server, and lets the nodes inside of it run code in that process. Remote Action Runs code in the external process of the Remote Client it is inside of and outputs the value the code assigned to result. Launch Process Starts a process that connects to the bridge server, like a headless application, waits for it and stops it when the nodes inside are done.

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
Runs its components when the flow reaches it. A general purpose step with a flow input and output.

Type id: core:action

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A general purpose step: the flow comes in, the node runs its components, the flow continues.
  • It has no other components. Add some to give it behavior, for example a Script.

docs.title: Branch
docs.text:
Continues through the true or false flow output depending on the condition value.

Type id: core:branch

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in Flow Execution flow into the node. true out Flow Flow that continues when the condition is true. false out Flow Flow that continues when the condition is false. condition in Boolean Value that chooses the output. Anything that isn't false, zero or empty counts as true.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The decision is made after the node is evaluated: only the chosen output is active, the nodes behind the other one don't run.
  • condition is read as a boolean. Anything that isn't false, zero or empty counts as true.
  • It has a flow input only. The outputs are true and false.

docs.title: Dict
docs.text:
Collects value components and creates a dictionary result.

Type id: core:dictionary

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description result out Dictionary Result dictionary

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Collects the value components of the node itself, keyed by the display name of each component.
  • Add Value components to it for the entries.
  • Add an Object Path component to point it at other nodes. Their value components are collected too.

docs.title: Flow Start
docs.text:
Marks where the execution flow of the parent scope begins.

Type id: core:flow_start

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has a single flow output and no input. The crawler looks for it in a scope and begins the execution there.
  • A scope without a Flow Start runs none of its children.

docs.title: For Each Loop
docs.text:
Runs the loop body for every element of an iterable, optionally in reverse, then continues with completed.

Type id: core:for_each_loop

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in Flow Execution flow into the node. iterable in Object Collection to go through, like a list or a string. reverse in Boolean Go through the elements from the last to the first. loop_body out Flow Flow that runs once for every element. element out Object Element of the current run of the loop body. index out Integer Position of the current element. completed out Flow Flow that continues after the last run of the loop body.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The chain linked to loop_body runs once for every element, then the flow continues through completed.
  • iterable can be a list, a string or anything else you can go through.
  • element and index are outputs. Link them to the nodes inside the body.

docs.title: For Loop
docs.text:
Runs the loop body for every index from the first to the last index, then continues with completed.

Type id: core:for_loop

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in Flow Execution flow into the node. first_index in Integer Index the loop starts with. last_index in Integer Index the loop ends with, this one included. loop_body out Flow Flow that runs once for every index. index out Integer Index of the current run of the loop body. completed out Flow Flow that continues after the last run of the loop body.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The chain linked to loop_body runs once for every index, then the flow continues through completed.
  • last_index is included: from 0 to 2 the body runs three times.
  • index is an output. Link it to the nodes inside the body.

docs.title: Get Type
docs.text:
Finds the type of an object when the flow reaches it.

Type id: core:get_type

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. object in Object Object to get the type of. type out Type Class of the object.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Finds the type when the flow reaches the node, and the flow continues.
  • The type output can be linked to the type of a Type Cast.

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
Provides the value of a component of another node.

Type id: core:get

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description component out Object Path Path of the component to read, like /stage/node.component. value out Object Value of the component the path points at.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has no flow component. It reads the component the path points at when something pulls its value.
  • component is a path like /stage/node.component, absolute or relative to the scope of the node.

docs.title: Launch Process
docs.text:
Starts a process that connects to the bridge server, like a headless application, waits for it and stops it when the nodes inside are done.

Type id: core:launch_process

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. command in String Command line to run. $NAME and ${NAME} are replaced by environment variables, the ones of env included. env in Dictionary Environment variables added to the ones of the application. working_directory in String Folder to run the command in. Empty uses the current one. client_name in String Name the process is to connect to the bridge as. Empty makes one up. wait_for_client in Boolean Wait until the process has connected before the nodes inside run. timeout in Float Seconds to wait for the process to connect before failing. 0 or less waits forever. client out String Name the process connects as. process_id out Integer Id of the process.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Acts as a scope: starts the process, runs the nodes inside of it, and stops the process when they are done.
  • In command, $NAME and ${NAME} are replaced by environment variables, the ones of env included.
  • With wait_for_client on, the nodes inside run only after the process has connected to the bridge as client_name.
  • Details: Remote nodes and the bridge.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
Collects value components and creates a list result.

Type id: core:list

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description result out List Result list

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Collects the value components of the node itself, in the order of the components.
  • Add Value components to it for the elements.
  • Add an Object Path component to point it at other nodes. Their value components are collected too, and come first.

docs.title: Log
docs.text:
Writes a message to the log with the chosen level.

Type id: core:log

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. message in String Text to write to the log. level in Integer Importance of the message as a logging level: 10 debug, 20 info, 30 warning, 40 error, 50 critical.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Writes the message to the log when the flow reaches the node, and the flow continues.
  • level is a Python logging level:
Level Name 10 debug 20 info 30 warning 40 error 50 critical

docs.title: Node
docs.text:
Empty node without components. Groups other nodes inside of it.

Type id: core:node

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has no components of its own. Its job is to be a scope: nodes created inside it are its children.
  • A node that contains children runs them with itself, after the node by default, starting from the Flow Start of its scope.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Stands for a stage file, with the components of its top node.

Type id: core:reference

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description source out String Stage file to reference, absolute or relative to the file of this stage.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Stands for another stage file. The components of the top node of that stage are shown on the node.
  • source is absolute or relative to the file of the stage that holds the reference.
  • What you can change, how it is saved and reloaded: see Referencing stages.

docs.title: Remote Action
docs.text:
Runs code in the external process of the Remote Client it is inside of and outputs the value the code assigned to result.

Type id: core:remote_action

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. script in String Python file or module:function entry point to run in the client. Assign the value to send back to result. args in Dictionary Variables the script can use, by name. timeout in Float Seconds to wait for the answer before failing. 0 or less waits forever. response out Object Value the script assigned to result.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has to be inside of a Remote Client. The script runs in the process of that client.
  • script is a Python file or a module:function entry point. Assign the value to send back to result: it comes out in response.
  • args are variables the script can use, by name.
  • Details: Remote nodes and the bridge.

docs.title: Remote Client
docs.text:
Waits for an external process to connect to the server, and lets the nodes inside of it run code in that process.

Type id: core:remote_client

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. client_name in String Name of the client to wait for. Empty accepts any, as long as only one client matches. client_kind in String Kind of the client to wait for, as it reports itself. Empty accepts any, as long as only one client matches. timeout in Float Seconds to wait for the client before failing. 0 or less waits forever. client out String Name of the connected client.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Acts as a scope: the nodes inside of it run code in the process that connects.
  • Waits for a client to connect to the bridge server. client_name and client_kind narrow down which one, empty accepts any as long as only one matches.
  • timeout of 0 or less waits forever.
  • Details: Remote nodes and the bridge.

docs.title: Sequence
docs.text:
Continues through all of its flow outputs one after another, in order.

Type id: core:sequence

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow_0 in / out Flow Execution flow into the node. flow_1 out Flow Flow that continues as step 1. flow_2 out Flow Flow that continues as step 2. flow_3 out Flow Flow that continues as step 3.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has one flow input, flow_0, and the outputs flow_1 to flow_3.
  • All outputs are active at once. Each one is followed completely, depth first, before the next one starts.

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
Sets the value of a component of another node when the flow reaches it.

Type id: core:set

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. component in Object Path Path of the component to change, like /stage/node.component. value in Object Value to set.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• component is the path of the component to change, like /stage/node.component. It is absolute, or relative to the scope of the node.
  • The value is written when the flow reaches the node, and the flow continues.

docs.title: Type Cast
docs.text:
Converts an object to the given type when the flow reaches it, e.g. a string to an int.

Type id: core:type_cast

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in / out Flow Connects the execution flow from one node to the next. type in Type Class to convert the object to. object in Object Object to convert. result out Object The object converted to the type.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Converts when the flow reaches the node, and the flow continues.
  • type is the class to convert to, for example int for a string with digits.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
Provides a value that can be edited and linked to other nodes.

Type id: core:value

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description value out Object Value of the node, it can be edited or linked.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Has no flow component. It runs when something pulls its value.
  • Edit the value on the node or link another component into it. Its datatype is Object until you pick another one, see Datatypes.
  • Use it to share one value between several nodes.

docs.title: While Loop
docs.text:
Runs the loop body for as long as the condition is true, then continues with completed.

Type id: core:while_loop

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Name Plug Datatype Description flow in Flow Execution flow into the node. condition in Boolean The loop body keeps running as long as this is true. loop_body out Flow Flow that runs while the condition is true. completed out Flow Flow that continues once the condition is false.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The chain linked to loop_body runs again and again while condition is true, then the flow continues through completed.
  • Something inside the body has to change the condition, for example with a Set, otherwise the loop never ends.

docs.title: Utility objects
docs.text:
Utility objects organize a graph. They don't execute.

Name What it does Note Sticky note with free text. Group Titled frame around nodes. Moving it moves the nodes inside.

docs.title: Group
docs.text:
Titled frame around nodes. Moving it moves the nodes inside.

Type id: core:group

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A titled frame behind the nodes it surrounds, to keep them together. Moving the group moves the nodes inside.
  • It doesn't execute. Create it with the Create group action (Ctrl+G).

docs.title: Note
docs.text:
Sticky note with free text.

Type id: core:note

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Free text on a coloured sticky note. It doesn't execute.
  • Create it with the Create note action.
